hook.text: Orange jumpsuits became standard in US prisons because they're impossible to blend into a crowd.

buildup.text: Stripping prisoners of personal clothing is a deliberate act of identity erasure. You become a number.

discovery.text: Nazi concentration camps used striped uniforms with colored badges—triangles coded race, religion, and crime.

twist.text: Some progressive prisons now let inmates wear personal clothes. Recidivism drops when identity survives incarceration.

climax.text: Guantánamo's orange jumpsuit became an iconic global symbol. ISIS used the same color on hostages as a reversal.

punchline.text: Controlling what someone wears controls who they are.

quiz.question: Why were orange jumpsuits chosen for US prisons?
